newsitem.title: UK: IKOS says launching new global hedge fund.
newsitem.headline: IKOS says launching new global hedge fund.

text.p: Hedge fund manager IKOS Partners said on Wednesday it was launching a global hedge fund taking positions in a wide range of major internationally traded futures contracts.
The new fund, the IKOS Global Fund, has been trading proprietary capital on these markets since April 1996, achieving returns in excess of 40 percent, it said.
Typically it would take long and short positions in stock indices, currencies, interest rate and bond futures focused on G7 economies.
The fund seeks a target annual return of 25 percent with 15 percent volatility based on a "broadly diversified portfolio and tight risk controls", it said.
It is modelled on the Japanese arbitrage hedge fund IKOS Offshore Arbitrage, which last month reached $100 million and is now closed to further investment.

"The global fund's trading strategy is based on a detailed analysis of the pricing levels of a wide range of futures contracts and is significantly different from most trading systems which rely on technical analysis and trend-following," IKOS said.

The model seeks valuation discrepancies, and the size of deviations are compared with the risk they contribute to the portfolio to determine trading sizes. Risk is reduced by diversifying positions among uncorrelated economic blocks.
"We expect to generate consistent returns over several years with moderate risk," said IKOS partner Martin Coward.
The Cayman Islands-registered fund is open-ended with a minimum $500,000 minimum subscription.
